extracted.intended_audience: Department of State bureaus, offices, and staff responsible for policies or activities that may have tribal implications; Department officials tasked with implementing E.O. 13175
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Department of State personnel on implementing Executive Order 13175 by planning, conducting, and following up on meaningful government-to-government consultation with federally recognized Indian tribes for policies that have tribal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: This Policy is intended to provide general guidance to Department bureaus and other components on policies with tribal implications.  It is not intended to, and does not, grant, expand, create, or diminish any legally enforceable rights, benefits, or trust responsibilities not otherwise granted or created under existing law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Policy to the extent permitted by law; do not interpret it as altering tribal sovereignty, treaty rights, or the Department's foreign affairs authority; update the Policy as engagements and circumstances dictate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental government-to-government commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends to continue to build stable and enduring relationships with Indian tribes by: meaningfully consulting in the development of regulatory policies that have tribal implications; consulting where appropriate on other proposed policies; engaging on a government-to-government basis; identifying liaisons; and working with other federal agencies to reduce duplicative information requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat tribes as separate sovereigns; recognize tribal diversity; honor legal/political relationships established by Constitution, treaties, statutes, and court decisions; designate liaisons to channel tribal inquiries; coordinate interagency engagement to minimize burdens on tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles guiding tribal engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends to be guided by general principles (Section V) emphasizing meaningful consultation, timely notification, solicitation of input, respectful ongoing communication, good faith, and taking tribal input into serious consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these principles flexibly to fit the range of issues; emphasize Department-wide commitment and sensitivity to international commitments (e.g., the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of commitment and timing of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirm the Department's commitment to engage in consultation with affected Tribal Governments and notify appropriate Tribal Governments of the Department's desire to engage in consultation in a timely manner.  Notice should be given as early in the decision-making process as possible, preferably in writing, and with sufficient detail about the proposed actions or policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information early enough for tribes to identify and evaluate implications and to participate meaningfully prior to decisions; use written notice when feasible; treat 'timely' as early in the decision-making process unless exigent circumstances apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active solicitation of input from potentially affected tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively solicit input from Tribal Governments identified as likely to be directly affected by the proposed policy, taking into account the scope of the policy, the timeline for decision-making, and other relevant criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the identification phase to determine which tribes are likely affected; prioritize outreach to those tribes and document the factors used to identify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of consultation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific manner in which the Department and Indian tribes engage in consultation should be flexible; consultation may warrant in-person meetings, virtual meetings, conference calls, or other mechanisms as determined by the Department to better foster productive communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select modalities (in-person, virtual, phone, written submissions, meetings at conferences, etc.) appropriate to the issue and tribes' needs; allow tribes to suggest procedures that accommodate their needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful, ongoing, good-faith communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain effective and respectful communication on an ongoing basis; promote coordination and cooperation with Indian tribes; and consult in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consultations are not merely perfunctory; give serious consideration to tribal input in decision-making and document how input influenced outcomes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal confidentiality and sensitive information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in tribal consultation in a manner that exhibits, to the greatest extent practicable and permitted by law, sensitivity to and respect for tribal confidentiality concerns regarding cultural, religious, political, and other intra-tribal affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with culturally sensitive locations, repatriation, or beliefs/practices, seek only the detail necessary for administrative decisions; be aware Department records are subject to disclosure laws but certain categories (e.g., location of archaeological sites) may be exempt from FOIA disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal requests for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation can be requested by the Department or by a Tribal Government; the Department will give serious consideration to a Tribal Government's request for consultation, taking into account the nature of the activity, past consultations, available resources, timing, and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat tribe-initiated requests seriously and assess feasibility and appropriateness; document decisions and rationales when declining or modifying consultation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability during consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain, to the extent permitted by relevant authorities and procedures, transparency and accountability throughout the consultation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear information to tribes about process, track consultations and outcomes, and be prepared to provide progress reports to OMB and other oversight entities as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-phase consultation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation generally consists of four phases: Identification, Notification, Input, and Follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the four-phase structure to plan consultations: identify whether consultation is needed and which tribes; notify with adequate info and lead time; solicit and receive input by appropriate methods; follow up with responses and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification phase criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant bureaus will consider whether proposed regulatory policies could have tribal implications, assess complexity, potential implications for Indian tribes, time/resource constraints, and identify potentially affected tribes if activity affects only certain tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reasonable possibility of tribal implications exists, engage in consultation to the greatest extent practicable (subject to exigent situations); document analysis of complexity, implications, and why tribes were identified or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative activities appropriate for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond regulatory policies, certain activities may be appropriate for consultation if they have tribal implications, e.g., Department involvement in international conferences on indigenous peoples; policies related to transboundary water or resource issues; implementation of U.S. obligations under international agreements that have tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the illustrative list to trigger consultation consideration for non-regulatory activities with potential tribal impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification phase requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify Indian tribes of proposed regulatory policies that have tribal implications and ensure affected tribes are adequately informed about the consultation process so they have the opportunity to participate or otherwise provide timely and meaningful input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification may occur by letter, email, telephone, Federal Register notice, or other reasonably effective means; include information necessary for tribes to decide whether to participate and aim to notify sufficiently early for meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input phase expectations and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no single formula for appropriate consultation; Department processes may include written and oral communications, phone calls, conference calls, in-person meetings, communications at conferences, and other interactions. The Department will coordinate with tribal officials to respond to requests for information and provide opportunities to give, receive, and discuss tribal input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer multiple avenues for input; be responsive to requests (including for technical experts); consider additional rounds of consultation when significant changes arise; ensure consultations allow an informed discussion of the proposed policy and tribal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of culturally sensitive site information
rubrics_metrics.description: When consulting to determine whether culturally sensitive locations may be affected, the Department will consider tribal desires to keep information confidential and will endeavor to obtain and record information only in the detail necessary to support administrative decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit collection/recording of location/details; inform tribes about potential public disclosure constraints and cite applicable FOIA exemptions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up phase obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will endeavor, as appropriate, to provide feedback and responses to Indian tribes who participated in the consultation and to respond, as appropriate, to points raised by tribes to the extent they were not responded to during the consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide written summaries of how input was considered, track unresolved issues, and follow up in a timely fashion; use follow-up to increase transparency and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of official with principal responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deputy Secretary for Management and Resources is the Department official with principal responsibility for the Department's implementation of E.O. 13175 and for maintaining the plan of action; bureaus should support that official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate and publicize the responsible official; ensure that official submits required reports to OMB and establishes mechanisms (e.g., a portal) for communications with Tribal Nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau-level points of contact and day-to-day implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Day-to-day implementation rests with the particular Department bureau, office, staff, post, or mission primarily responsible for the proposed policy; each such entity should designate a point of contact once consultation is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureaus must name POCs, ensure they are resourced to coordinate consultations, and coordinate internally or jointly when responsibility is shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working groups for consultation planning and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Any bureau, office, or staff may convene a working group comprised of Department employees from across relevant bureaus, offices, posts, and missions, and of employees from other federal agencies as appropriate, to plan, coordinate, and follow up on a consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use working groups to centralize expertise, ensure consistent messaging, and coordinate multi-jurisdictional or multi-issue consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA inapplicability to tribal consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) do not apply to consultations under this Policy; FACA is not applicable to consultations between the federal government and elected officers of Tribal Governments (or their designated employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat tribal government consultations as subject to FACA requirements; document legal basis for FACA inapplicability when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: policies that have tribal implications
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Policies that have tribal implications’ refers to regulations, legislative comments or proposed legislation, and other policy statements or actions that have substantial direct effects on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this definition when deciding whether to initiate the identification and notification phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policymaking criteria: respect sovereignty and defer to tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall respect Indian tribal self-government and sovereignty, honor tribal treaty and other rights, and strive to meet responsibilities arising from the federal-tribal relationship. Where possible, grant tribes maximum administrative discretion, encourage tribes to develop their own policies, defer to tribal standards, and consult with tribal officials regarding the need for Federal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer tribal-led solutions and preserve tribal prerogatives when formulating policies; document reasons when federal standards are proposed instead of tribal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special requirement: legislative proposals consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall not submit to the Congress legislation that would be inconsistent with the policymaking criteria in Section 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review legislative proposals for consistency with tribal sovereignty, discretion, and consultation principles before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory preconditions for rules imposing substantial direct compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent practicable and permitted by law, no agency shall promulgate any regulation that has tribal implications, that imposes substantial direct compliance costs on Indian tribal governments, and that is not required by statute, unless: (1) funds necessary to pay the direct costs are provided by the Federal Government; or (2) the agency consulted early, provided a tribal summary impact statement to OMB describing prior consultation and tribal concerns and the agency's position, and made available to OMB any written communications submitted by tribal officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing costly regulations affecting tribes, either secure funding to cover tribal costs or document early consultation, summarize impacts and concerns in the preamble to the regulation, and submit tribal communications to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on preempting tribal law
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent practicable and permitted by law, no agency shall promulgate any regulation that has tribal implications and that preempts tribal law unless the agency consulted with tribal officials early, provided a tribal summary impact statement to OMB, and made available to OMB any written communications submitted by tribal officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid preemption of tribal law where possible; when preemption is contemplated, document early consultation and provide the tribal summary impact statement and supporting materials to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consensual mechanisms (negotiated rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: On issues relating to tribal self-government, tribal trust resources, or treaty and other rights, each agency should explore and, where appropriate, use consensual mechanisms for developing regulations, including negotiated rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider negotiated rulemaking or other consensus-based approaches for sensitive, sovereignty-related issues; document exploration and rationale for chosen rulemaking mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver processes and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall review processes under which tribes apply for waivers of statutory/regulatory requirements and streamline those processes; consider waiver applications with a view toward increasing flexible policy approaches; render a decision upon a complete application within 120 days, or provide timely written notice of denial and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this section only to discretionary statutory/regulatory requirements subject to waiver; establish internal procedures to meet the 120-day target and notify applicants in writing when denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability: certifications and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: When transmitting any draft final regulation or proposed legislation that has tribal implications to OMB, agencies shall include a certification from the official designated to ensure compliance with this order stating that the requirements of the order have been met in a meaningful and timely manner; OMB and the Assistant to the President for Intergovernmental Affairs shall confer with tribal officials to ensure proper implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure designated officials sign required certifications; maintain records demonstrating how consultation requirements were met for OMB review and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent agencies encouraged to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent regulatory agencies are encouraged to comply with the provisions of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage independent agencies as partners and encourage adoption of similar consultation practices even if not legally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and updating of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends to review this Policy from time to time, in consultation with Tribal Governments, in order to make any revisions as may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule periodic reviews, solicit tribal feedback on the Policy's effectiveness, and publish updates as appropriate; submit required implementations/reports to OMB as called for in the Presidential Memorandum.
